title: Cinna
tagline: Real-time bus tracking for Cyprus public transit.
description: Case study: Cinna — real-time bus tracking for all seven Cyprus bus operators. Flutter on iOS and Android over Django, PostGIS and a dedicated GTFS-RT fetcher; 14 ADRs, 1,400+ tests.
lede: A live map of every bus in Cyprus, arrival estimates you can trust, and a trip planner that would rather say “I don’t know” than guess. Flutter on iOS and Android, over a Django and PostGIS backend fed by the national real-time feed.
alt: A folded transit map on a dark desk with one route traced in cobalt thread, a brass token beside it.

meta.Stack: Flutter · Riverpod · Django REST · PostGIS · Celery · Redis
meta.Status: Backend in production · iOS pilot on TestFlight

card.problem: Public-transit riders are stuck with schedules that drift from reality and clunky paper-or-card ticketing — no single place to see where the bus actually is and pay for the ride.
card.approach: A real-time transit companion: a Flutter/Riverpod app for iOS and Android over a Django REST + PostGIS backend that ingests the national GTFS-RT feed every 15 seconds — plus Stripe tickets delivered as Apple/Google Wallet passes.
bullets: A dedicated fetcher writes live positions straight into PostGIS — current state and history in separate tables.
PostGIS for spatial work — nearest-stop, route geometry, “arriving near me”.
Arrival estimates designed to say “unknown” rather than be confidently wrong.
Every significant call written down — 14 architecture decision records.
card.outcome: Backend in production, iOS pilot on TestFlight, 1,400+ automated tests. Private repo — walkthrough on request.
links: Private · demo on request

title: Ludi
tagline: Football pitch booking and matchmaking for Cyprus.
description: Case study: Ludi, a two-sided marketplace for five-a-side football in Cyprus. A player app, a Greek owner dashboard and a lobby TV on one Postgres database, where double-booking is impossible by construction.
lede: Book a five-a-side pitch in a few taps, fill the team with an open match, and give venue owners a calendar instead of a WhatsApp thread. A player app, an owner dashboard in Greek and a lobby TV, all on one Postgres database.
alt: A worn leather football on a dark desk beside a referee’s whistle and a booking card with one slot stamped in cobalt.

meta.Stack: Expo / React Native · Next.js · Supabase (Postgres, PostGIS, RLS) · Stripe Connect
meta.Status: Launched · iOS app approved · payments in test mode

card.flag_html: Live
card.role: Solo · Expo + Next.js + Supabase · Apr – Oct 2026
card.problem: Five-a-side in Cyprus runs on WhatsApp: players chase pitches and people through group chats, and owners keep the calendar in their heads.
card.approach: A two-sided marketplace. A player app to find a pitch, book, pay and fill the team; a Greek owner dashboard to run the week; and a lobby TV. All three sit on one Postgres database.
bullets: Double-booking is impossible by database constraint: of 100 simultaneous bookings, exactly one wins.
Row-level security on every table, covered by 249 pgTAP tests.
Card payments and venue payouts through Stripe Connect, built end to end.
card.outcome: Launched in August, with the iOS app approved by Apple and early partner venues on the dashboard. Payments are in test mode until going live.

title: Aristophanes
tagline: An end-to-end platform for theatre, from solo practice to running a production.
description: Case study: Aristophanes, an end-to-end platform for theatre companies. It grew from a scene partner for one actor into a production space with roles, call board, calendar, wardrobe and box office. Built in Flutter (iOS and Android) on Supabase with row-level security, and documented in 62 ADRs.
lede: It began as a scene partner for one actor rehearsing Lysistrata alone. Then a director asked for the whole company. Today it is a platform for theatre: each production gets its own space, with roles that mirror the org chart, a call board, a rehearsal calendar, a shared wardrobe and a box office, and every actor still has a partner to rehearse with.
alt: A graphite hexagonal block with aluminium adapter plugs around it, one seated and ringed in cobalt light.

meta.Stack: Flutter (iOS + Android) · Supabase + RLS · Riverpod · Drift · Next.js · Stripe
meta.Status: In use by a 12-person cast · Lampblack redesign in testing

card.role: Solo · Flutter (iOS + Android) + Supabase · May – Sep 2026
card.problem: Amateur theatre runs on paper scripts and group chats: actors rehearse alone, and directors juggle schedules, costumes and casting across a dozen threads.
card.approach: An end-to-end platform for theatre: each production is its own space, with roles that mirror the org chart, a call board, calendar, shared wardrobe and box office, plus a scene partner for every actor. It began as a rehearsal app for one actor.
bullets: Seven production roles: the app shows the right buttons, and row-level security is the only server boundary.
Eight versions in eight days took it from one actor to a whole company, with security tested live.
62 ADRs, and a full design-system pass (Lampblack) before restyling any screen.
card.outcome: In use by a 12-person cast; 829 automated tests. Private repo, walkthrough on request.
links: Private · demo on request

title: Wiseprint
tagline: A cost-plus pricing engine that became a print shop’s working tool.
description: Case study: Wiseprint, pricing and job management for a one-store print shop in Cyprus. A pure cost-plus engine, immutable quotes and a self-updating install on the shop’s Mac. 45 versions, 2,518 tests.
lede: A print shop priced every job in the owner’s head. Wiseprint prices it the way he already does (paper, printing, finishing, margin), keeps every quote as a frozen record, and grew into the shop’s job board, intake and press queue. It’s in Greek, at the counter and on his phone.
alt: A stack of business cards with one cobalt-painted edge, a paper swatch fan, a calculator and a brass ruler on a dark desk.

meta.Status: In daily use at the shop

card.flag_html: Private
card.role: Solo · for a print shop · Django + HTMX · Sep 2026
card.problem: A print shop priced every job in the owner’s head and kept enquiries on paper, so no job could ever be rebuilt from a record.
card.approach: A cost-plus pricing engine that prices the way the owner already does, grown into the shop’s job board, intake and press queue. It’s in Greek, on the counter PC and his phone.
bullets: A pure engine with no framework imports, its answers worked out by hand in 26 cases before the code existed.
Saved quotes are frozen with a fingerprint of the rates they used, so a price change never rewrites history.
It updates itself from a release branch on the shop’s own Mac, with nightly off-site backups.
card.outcome: In daily use at the shop, across 45 owner-approved versions and 2,518 tests. Private repo, walkthrough on request.
links: Private · walkthrough on request

title: Plutarch
tagline: Ρίζα — an open dictionary of Modern Greek where every definition cites its source.
description: Case study: Plutarch (Ρίζα), an open Modern Greek dictionary — 95,774 entries from Greek Wiktionary, accent-insensitive search over 650k inflected forms, built in four days on Next.js and Postgres.
lede: Ρίζα is an open dictionary of Modern Greek where every definition carries a citation you can click through to. Type any form of a word — accented or not, monotonic or polytonic — and land on its entry, with declension and conjugation tables, cross-references and real usage examples.
alt: An open antique lexicon on a dark desk with a brass loupe resting on the page and a cobalt ribbon bookmark.

meta.Status: Live at plutarch-five.vercel.app

card.problem: Greek dictionaries online are slow and shallow — hard to scan, weak on cross-references, painful to explore a word's neighbourhood.
card.approach: Ρίζα, an open Modern Greek dictionary: 95,774 entries from Greek Wiktionary, with accent-insensitive search that resolves any inflected form to its entry — Next.js + TypeScript over Postgres.
bullets: Structured, normalised entries so meanings and relations are first-class, not free text.
Server-rendered Next.js for fast, shareable, search-friendly pages.
card.outcome: Live, built in four days, 98 tests. Source private for now.
